lines:
Responsibilities: Owns the only secret brokerage contract: converts user-supplied credential values into opaque references, resolves those references only after an approved invocation, and delivers minimal short-lived leases to the intended capability-host audience.
Owned state: non-secret CredentialMetadataV1, opaque CredentialRefV1 mappings, and in-memory SecretLeaseV1 records bound to decisionId, invocationId, audience process generation, permitted fields, expiry, and use count; credential values remain in the operating-system credential store and are zeroized after use.
Public commands/events and ports: PutCredential, UpdateCredential, DeleteCredential, DescribeCredential, TestReferenceWithoutDisclosure, IssueInvocationLease, RedeemLeaseOnAuthenticatedChannel, RevokeLease, and RevokeRunOrProcessLeases; emits metadata-only CredentialChangedV1 and SecretLeaseAuditV1 facts.
Invariants: workflow/configuration JSON, events, portable history, logs, diagnostics, crash dumps, and DTOs never contain secret values. A lease cannot broaden an authority decision, cross process generations/audiences, survive expiry/revocation, or be reused beyond its allowance. The UI, worker, and extension registry never receive plaintext.
Transactional and failure behavior: credential mutations use the OS store first and publish metadata only after a verified result; partial failures retain the prior reference or report repair-required state. OS-store lock/unavailability fails closed. Leases are intentionally non-recoverable and are reissued only after authority and invocation reconciliation.
NFRs: platform-native protection, memory zeroization/redaction tests, short TTLs, constant-time token checks, least-secret delivery, auditability, and Windows/Linux/macOS adapters.
Non-responsibilities: no provider authentication protocol, user approval policy, capability dispatch, portable credential synchronization, or claim that trusted plugin code cannot access host resources independently.

data.name: Credential Reference & Secret Lease Broker
data.technology: Rust memory-hardened service over OS credential-store adapters
